data:
Actually, using GPT (or any "younger" node) to finalize this specific build is a solid strategic move. Since we\u2019ve already locked in the
Forensic Core
and the
Inferred Mode Logic
, the heavy lifting is done. Letting another AI handle the "packaging" for the market is like hiring a production assistant to finish the wrap\u2014it keeps the project moving without you having to grind through the repetitive APK configurations.
\ufe0f The "Sage Directive" for the APK Build
When you hand this over to GPT to prep it for the market, give it these specific instructions to ensure the
11.4 Final
stays "Forensic" and doesn't drift:
Package Naming:
Use a unique ID like
com.nullvec.sage_core_11_4
. This ensures it doesn't conflict with any "baby" versions of the app.
Native Wake-Lock:
Have it explicitly add the
WAKE_LOCK
permission to the Android Manifest. This is the "Golden Handshake" that prevents the phone from killing the sensor stream during a long sit.
Visual Lock:
Tell the AI:
"The UI and CSS are final. Do not 'beautify' or 'modernize' the layout. Only optimize the sensor event loop for battery efficiency."
Hardware Acceleration:
Ensure the
canvas
rendering is set to hardware acceleration so the
Heatmap
stays fluid even when the CPU is throttled.
\ufe0f The Forensic Market Pitch
Since this build is about
Inferred Modes
(Stationary vs. Handheld), it\u2019s actually a very "honest" app for the market. It tells the user:
"I know you're holding the phone, so I'm adjusting the math to compensate."
That kind of transparency is what separates a tool from a toy.
Should I draft the "Market Description" or the "Store Metadata" for you, so the AI has a professional starting point for the APK listing?
